correctness.rationale: The cited Theorem 5.2 provides monotone unique irrational inverse parameters and rational plateau intervals. A direct Möbius derivative gives strictly positive uniform conversion of rational S-jumps to parameter gaps. The series truncation has exponential tail on any u<=rho<=v<r, with a proven lower bound 1-lambda on all denominators; finite Sturmian floor sums have O(N^2) rational transition cells, yielding O(log(1/epsilon)^2) covers. Every reduced p/q with q<=Q has a plateau of length at least C*s_*^q, and the Farey asymptotic gives Theta(Q^2) mutually epsilon-separated intermediate irrational parameters when Q scales with log(1/epsilon). Exact-rational replay: 7,139 assertions. Tests are supplementary and do not replace the universal argument. Endpoints outside compact windows are explicitly excluded from the box-count assertion.

value.rationale: The natural number of equal-resolution parameter intervals needed to distinguish aperiodic irrational-rotation states has sharp logarithmic exponent two, while ordinary fractal dimensions vanish. Matching upper/lower control is not a routine restatement of zero Hausdorff dimension or of gauge estimates. The theorem quantifies the Farey-tongue complexity of near-aperiodic parameters, and extends the quantitative exceptional-set theory from branchwise-contractive maps to explicit systems with a right-branch expansion factor 3/2.
